reviews.text: love having to deal with really finnicky controls, performance issues, the ranger class being essentially unplayable, thrown weapons being unusuable, dual weapons randomly stopping shooting, and enemies that start and finish attack windup in one frame just to get a "please review us hehe" message pop up in my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ face after 2 runs. I REALLY want to love this but I LITERALLY CANNOT REBIND AND BUTTONS so I am FORCED to jump with joystick up. Edit: They also have a roadmap with PERFORMANCE FIXES on it. Roboquest could have been a native VR game, but Flat2VR Studios did something great here by taking the original flat game and reworking every weapon of the game and giving full 6DOF movement for all the weapons, yet they preserved the original design of the game with the player movement and balance, while giving the players multiple options for the weapon reload mechanic: Can do a quick reload with a button press similar to the flat game, or full 3D two handed gesture reload like a native VR title. And for those who have not played the original game it's like playing a native VR port, not just a 'lazy VR conversion'. If you own the flat version, I have not tested to see if the flat save game is compatible with the VR version, but no matter as it's 100% worth playing the game and unlocking everything again in VR. Now I just need to work on unlocking all the robo classes now :) Disclaimer: I was provided a copy of the game for testing purposes, but it does not affect my review.

I wish I could give Robotquest VR a 'neutral' rating until a couple of things get added, but it's still far more positive than negative. This game deserves to be noticed and I want to support the Flat2VR developers. The port is great quality and feels like it was made for VR, it has the potential to be a huge amount of fun and there's a ton of good content here, I feel the price justifies the time they've worked on it and what you can get out of it. Granted, it is very intense. I tend to not move my head or turn my body much in VR, but I stayed in it for 3 hours, trying both standing and sitting, and my body feels bruised. I did finally manage to get to and beat the boss of the first zone before failing near the start of the second. The only technical issue I had was a white screen for a bit when going to the second zone, during a loading screen which I could see on my PC monitor in passthrough, but I managed to get past it. My primary demerit with the current state of the game is the lack of customizable controls/keybinds. It's great that it does come with multiple accessibility options, but there is no excuse for lack of key customization in 2025 in a released game. Not everyone is equally abled. I spent as much time fighting with my controller as the infected robots, which quickly makes it feel unfair and unfun, especially when that prevents me from progression because I hit the wrong buttons when I can't adapt to someone else' ability or preferences. The Steam Frame is being released soon with a more typical xbox layout, so this needs to be prioritized if you want to make sales there. There needs to at least be a tutorial for throwing weapons, as it took me nearly 10 minutes to figure out how the controls work for them. Possibly they could benefit from some kind of autofire setting. They are fun, but much harder to aim than the guns as well as not having sight lines, to the point that I probably couldn't win runs with them. I actually had no issue using the Ranger's Javelin, but that seems to have a fair bit of autoaim on top. And of course, the lack of co-op at launch is a bit sad as that's what PCVR sorely needs to make it a popular system seller. I really hope that the VR version will support crossplay with the flatscreen versions which already support crossplay. I have friends who play Roboquest in flatscreen but don't have PCVR setups or don't want to play it in VR.

This game is kind of like a rougelike, where every time you start a match you get different rarity weapons that do different things, like a boomerang or rocket launchers. There's also different card you get per level that increase damage, or your shield, gives you a special effects etc, in order to help you in your current run. I had a blast playing this game, it filled the itch I had to play a rougelike game, and what made it fun was that it was in and somewhat difficult too. The bosses you fight are amazing, like the first one I get obliterated but was able to get it to half health by learning it's patterns, which felt so immersive because I was dodging and weaving in real life, just the VR aspect in general is super fun. The only downside I found was that the maps themselves weren't randomly generated like the weapons were, since the game follows a story line, so it kind of like your playing chapters but not at the same time, cant really find the right words for it. But other than that it's an amazing game, and see a lot of potential for it be because a top tier VR game!
If you're looking for a fast paced shooter with deep advancement mechanics in VR this is it!
Few lag spikes here and there, but game is fast paced and fun! Hope to see some cross play multiplayer with the flatscreen version someday.

I'm seriously impressed with this game. I am a HUGE fan of the flatscreen version and know I was going to like this regardless as I have been craving a game like this on VR for ages. I was blown away at how well done the "port" was. It feels native to VR. The movement was my biggest concern and after half an hour its starting to click. If you enjoy anything this game offers buy it. It's well worth 30 bucks. To the devs: Sorry for not posting a review sooner, you where on 69 reviews and I didn't want to ruin it :P

The game itself is pretty addicting. It's fast-paced, has some pretty good roguelike modifiers - just an overall satisfying gameplay loop and is worth the asking price with it being originally a full blown flat screen game but can be quite the disappointment if you're looking to fully utilize the features of this medium shift. What irks me is that the devs spent a ton of time giving a large number of guns manual reload only to make manual reload WAY too optional. Most games tend to balance out using manual reloading by giving you certain buffs like more damage or even mag size. But this game just doesn't. I'm pretty sure that most players will just opt out of using the manual reload to go for the more effective auto reload feature. And also, the laser pointer targeting sights are VERY distracting. I prefer playing with it turned off, but I eventually caved because, again, there's just nothing in terms of balancing to give you an incentive to actually aim your shots without any guidance. Also, there's very little benefit of 2-handing weapons since all of them are VERY usable using one hand. I feel like 2-handing them just gives a 10-20% recoil reduction, and since the base recoil is very much tolerable, there's no incentive to 2-hand stuff. What I would love is if the devs gave at least a 10 or 20% mag size increase if you have manual reloading and maybe a 10% damage increase if you turn off the laser pointer. The hard work has been done, now encourage us to use those features. I'm giving this game a thumbs down. I just feel that all the effort and work the devs put into this were just wasted and in the end, it's not much of an upgrade over a modded base game using the UEVR injector. But don't get me wrong, it's a helluva fun time if you don't care about manual reloading or don't mind using the laser pointer. Please devs, could you give us an incentive to use manual reload and turn off the laser pointer? That would actually make this pretty much one of the best titles in this space due to its high replay value.

I want to start off with saying that I am a huge fan of Roboquest. It’s easily one of the best rogue-likes I’ve ever played. So, it's a little jarring for me to leave this review of not recommending this VR port. My main complaint is lack of binding controls. At the moment it’s a little rough to get into this game if you require certain inputs to be bound in your preferred control scheme. The default controls aren’t so good. Important inputs such as jump and crouch bound to joystick will always be a minus for me. Lack of leaning into the platform. This game sticks too close to the desktop version of the game and I would’ve loved to see things lean into VR as a platform more. What I mean is maybe adding new content such as guns, tiles and customizables that would add more charm to the overall experience to differentiate this VR port from the desktop game a little. It’s just Roboquest, but more expensive and in VR. Not Roboquest but helped by VR and pushed to the next level. But all hope is not lost. The devs need to cook a little longer on this and as a Roboquest fan I am anxiously awaiting the next couple of updates to see what they are bringing to the table. I’m assuming they meant to release this in early access as even the released version isn’t a “1.0” version. It’s clear they ran out of time. The lack of multiplayer on release is a bit disappointing but I’m hoping they can have customizable bindings and multiplayer soon. If these two things can be done it’ll go a long way to improve my opinion of this vr port. In the meanwhile if people ask me which version they should pickup I will have to point them towards the desktop version of the game for now until the VR version is finished. Edit 1: Removed my comments on throwing weapons. I have been told it has been fixed through comments and the official patch announcements though I haven't tried it myself. Hopefully it's indeed better and people are having fun throwing javelins. Edit 2: They also seemed to have fixed the angle adjustments on aiming to be for both axis. Originally it was only locked to vertical adjustment but they added horizontal adjustment. Good fix!

The devs did an insanely good job bringing the game into VR, nothing feels half-ported or compromised. The guns feel fantastic to shoot, super punchy and satisfying in the hands, and the soundtrack, noisecream absolutely melts your brain in the best way possible. The whole thing just vibes perfectly in VR. All the core mechanics are here and they’re implemented really well. Movement feels smooth, gunplay is tight, and the overall flow is just pure adrenaline. A few downsides, though: Optimization isn’t perfect yet. I’m on a 3080 Ti + 9700K @ 4.9GHz + 32GB RAM, and fps drops after 3rd or 4th biome. Running on low settings for stable performance, which isn’t ideal. Only one default control layout. I’m sure you can tweak things through Steam, but I’d love a couple of official alternatives out of the box. Spears still feel weird to throw — probably something you get used to, but still a bit clunky. No multiplayer yet (can’t wait to play co-op). Honestly, even with these issues, the game is an absolute blast. Super promising, super fun, and already worth every minute. If you love fast-paced VR shooters, this one is a must-try.

[h1]Experienced on the Meta Quest 3[/h1] You can view my full review here: https://youtu.be/vZrskdRetM0 This is a great VR game that I highly recommend. In my opinion, it should have been nominated for VR GOTY 2025. This is a unique game in VR because of it's fast-paced gameplay, combining quick shooting with running, jumping, and sliding, along with the smart use of special abilities. There's so many weapons, different upgrades, and 6 (soon to be 7) classes to choose from, each with unique abilities, changing up the play-style. I would say this game is perfect for VR veterans who are unphased by the fast-movement. Now, everything isn't perfect. This is a VR port of a game that was probably never intended to be played in VR. As such, the VR mechanics don't always align 100% with the frenetic style or control scheme. However, I think the devs did the best with the difficult choices they had to make to bring this to VR. In the end, you have a very unique game in VR that no mod can duplicate and to which a VR first title is unlikely to ever birth. I had a blast playing this. I had to turn on auto-run because my hands were starting to hurt because of all the required running and gunning. Game is running on the Unreal Engine 4. On my RTX 5090, I was getting mostly 90 fps (on almost max graphical settings). You have full locomotion, along with smooth and snap turning. You can play comfortably seated. Rate 8/10. 好玩！潜力很大 但是很可惜我要给个差评 原版我也玩了挺久了，作为一个肉鸽射击游戏还是蛮好玩的，而且高机动性枪械手感也不错打的很爽。vr版几乎是照搬过来的，简单尝试了一会，说一下我的体验给大家做个参考（因为游戏暂时还没有达到我的预期所以我要先退款，后面更新了再购入，所以我的游戏时间不长，体验仅供参考） 1.首先一个缺点就是汉化不完善，后面的各项肉鸽卡牌内容我还没打到不清楚汉化怎么样（目前遇到的肉鸽选项倒是都汉化了）反正教程和设置基本上只汉化了30%左右，我觉得教程和设置难道不是更新后几乎不会改动的文本吗，难道不应该最先做本地化吗？教程是每个玩家都要过的，设置更是很多玩家都会选择先进去过一遍并且直接影响到了玩家整个游戏的体验，这点不做本地化，虽然内容少玩家可以自己解决但是很影响刚入手游戏的第一印象 并且汉化还有个问题是在语言设置里竟然没有？？默认语言是空白，点开列表进去只有其他7种语言没有中文，如果不小心选择了其他的语言就改不回来中文了，只能重置所有的设置为默认再重启游戏（刚开始没发现这个方法我差点以为改不回去了） 2.本体是有联机的，但是我看steam商店只有单人tag，我还以为是vr做联机难度高就被砍了，但是进到游戏里会发现有多人模式的选项，点进去是coming soon，也就是说制作组后续还是会更新多人模式，那很棒了，这种游戏多人的乐趣会翻几倍并且游戏寿命也会大大增加，我记得本体已经停更了吧，希望制作组加紧更新的脚步 3.优化稀烂稀烂稀烂，原版优化很好，而且这种卡通渲染风格也确实不吃性能，但是为什么你vr版优化可以这么烂？我4070s 12700 32g的配置极高画面设置在基地竟然只有60多帧，高画质只有7 80左右，只有开中才能有90，进战斗依然会掉帧。并且本身游戏就糊，开极高都有锯齿和模糊，开中更是散光800度一样，能玩，但是折磨眼睛 4.图鉴的设定，这一点在原版就想吐槽了，你拿到一把武器或者遇到敌人，图鉴里只会解锁他的剪影图标和名字，想解锁信息需要用武器击杀230人，然后解锁了点进去也只有武器的伤害射速弹匣等几项基础信息，敌人更是只能看到模型没有任何信息。这是生怕玩家没什么玩，让玩家去刷特定武器和敌人吗 5.原版的枪械手感还算不错，但是在vr里就很差（虽然确实vr的手感很难做，这是很多小体量vr游戏的通病，但是这游戏还是感觉很奇怪） 抛开手感这一点谈谈其他的，首先这游戏的后座不高，但是依然会持续上抬，并且双手武器并不能通过抓住前握把来减少甚至抵消后坐力，也就是说一把步枪我单手拿和双手拿只有左手是否影响枪口指向的问题，那我为什么不直接单手开枪，又准又舒服？ 并且只能右手拿枪，左手闲的没事干，你都vr了，改一改双持不好吗，原版那个不好用的双枪直接取消掉好了。稍微加强一下后座，让步枪类武器需要双手持枪才能打得准，再加个双持，让手枪冲锋枪之类的武器可以双持打得爽，这不是挺合理的吗，甚至还可以出一点vr专属的双枪游侠角色或者技能卡牌之类的 6.也是武器的问题，换弹非常别扭导致我只用自动换弹 游戏里有两种模式，自动和手动，自动就是和原版一样，按a自动播放动画然后一段时间后换弹完毕，或者打空弹匣会自动换弹。自动就是按a弹出弹匣然后左手抓握键可以虚空抓一个弹匣插进去，并且这游戏没有空仓挂机和膛内一发弹，所以就算打空了弹匣也只需要直接换个弹匣并不需要拉栓就可以直接开枪，这在一个快节奏的游戏里对于手动换弹来说是一个挺好的设定 手动换弹这样听着没有什么问题对不对？但是最大的问题在于，他不能像其他游戏一样，左手先抓一个弹匣然后卸掉枪上面的弹匣秒插进去换弹，因为需要先弹出旧弹匣，然后大概半秒之后才可以抓取新的弹匣插进去，并且插进去之后还会有莫名其妙的延迟（或者说后摇？）之后才能开火，也就是说即使你手动换弹也要等待和自动换弹一样的时间才能开火。你tm又不是电竞游戏，你搁这学习隔壁BreacherVR呢，人家pvp你也pvp吗？隔壁守护者前线是采用了手动换弹增加一倍弹容量并且加25%的伤害作为激励，并且熟练的话手动换弹在不需要拉栓的情况下几乎可以秒换，你哪怕不改动伤害和弹容，你在腰上放个弹匣然后取消换弹的硬直，让玩家熟练之后可以比自动更快的换弹作为激励这样不好吗，否则的话在一款快节奏游戏玩家为了过关只能选择自动换弹，比较影响沉浸感 （因为我只短暂体验了一下所以只玩了几把武器，还没玩到后面的各种 复合弓 加特林 加农炮 离子拳 这些奇怪的武器，所以暂时不谈论这些武器的手动换弹方式） 7.希望能增加按键选择，目前右手承担了大部分操作，拿枪 瞄准 开枪 放技能 近战 放枪械技能 跳跃 转向，而左手基本只负责移动，所以经常会出现右手噼里啪啦按不过来，换弹跳跃技能一起放一个大拇指搁那跟自己打架，然后左手就悬空一直按住左移的情况 8.投掷类的武器希望能增加吸附效果，本来投掷就又慢又累，还经常打不中敌人，毕竟是vr游戏，希望可以给一点辅助 其他小问题的话，就是老生常谈的vr眩晕症的问题了，这个确实没太大办法解决，我个人还是不太晕的，不过在高机动下玩久了还是有点不舒服，不过好在游戏的四档难度可以自选，选个简单点的慢慢打也可以 补充一点我在游戏里看到版本是0.9几，看来还没到制作组预期的1.0版本，但是这一点steam商店并没有标注，并且meta商店里的一体机版本依然还没有发售，看起来制作组确实是把steam版当做一个抢先体验，希望制作组能尽快更新各种问题吧 后续各种内容优化好了我会买回来改回好评的

One of the best (unplayable) games ever, but......... imagine holding a firearm in real life, but if you grip the handle it VANISHES INTO THIN AIR. How exactly are you imagining an intuitive comfort in NOT BEING ALLOWED TO GRIP YOUR CONTROLLER WHEN AIMING THE GUN? IF I GRIP MY GUN, IT TURNS INTO A FIST?!?! I thought there was a tracking issue for a moment that kept making my gun disappear until I realized I'm expected to release my controller, but use the trigger, while aiming.. It's so... wrong, so so so so so wrong. I'd unfortunately mentally categorize this as unplayable, because if you go through with this, your brain is going to get zero pleasure out of a gripless trigger firing mechanism, not to mention your brain will form a broken schema that makes you question what you can and can't do while playing other immersive shooters, it's not worth rewiring yourself in a way that literally doesn't make sense in the first place. -==PLEASE FIX THIS IMMEDIATELY, IT'S LITERALLY POINTLESS TO GO FORWARDS IN DEVELOPMENT WITHOUT CHANGING SOMETHING ABOUT THIS, others have had complaints about not being able to change controls as well, but this one is particularly game ruining. NO STABLE CONTROLLABLE AIM? NO ACTUAL GAME.==- I don't want to rant about the nuances where this ruins the entire experience of trying to be mobile or have actual fun, but you get it, it's a destructive formula that doesn't work. I didn't have any other complaints personally, but that single issue is beyond insane if you are a human using the Valve Index right now. If you say skill issue you are just willing to compromise a 11/10 gaming experience for a gaslight arguing point that ends with the game potentially remaining 2/10 in its current state instead of being improved dramatically with a singular fix.

Having put some time into the flatscreen version, I can say from what I've played that Roboquest VR is a really well done port. Gunplay still feels fast and exciting and this version puts you right there in the action. From what I can see everything from the flatscreen version has made it across, from the classes with their varied abilites, to the range of gadgets that can expand your movement options further. Some changes have obviously been made to make it more intuitive for Virtual Reality. The option to choose between manual and single button reloading is a nice addition, as is the fact that throwing weapons lock on to enemies, so you don't need to try predicting your angles in the middle of combat. All the standard VR options are there from seated mode to dominant hand selection and movement stick selection. As a left-handed player who also moves with the left stick, that was very nice to see. Button prompts also seemed to match correctly once I swapped everything as well, which was a pleasant surprise compared to other games I've played in the past. Something not so great though, is that heavy weapons like the minigun and flamethrower seem to flip out when gripping with two hands and make it impossible to aim. I'm assuming this is either a bug or unintended interaction that will hopefully get fixed very soon. Keeping that in mind though, if you're looking for a fast-paced VR Roguelite with a ton of varied weapons and upgrades, this is definitely one to consider and if you're a fan of the flatscreen version then I would say it's worth picking up.

[h3]That's how you do a VR FPS Rogue-lite[/h3] Alright, do you already know Roboquest ? I did try it and loved it during a previous Steam Next Fest and enjoyed the demo. However, now we have a VR version of it. And it really changes how the game handles. You get to take even more enjoyment handling combos of robot kills with your weapons and skillfully dash and run around, bumping on robots heads to defeat them. Either with a revolver, automatic dual SMGs, throwing knives and hatchets, pistols, or flamethrowers, and I'm missing a lot. My favorite? ABSOLUTELY THE BOW. From playing The Lab a lot, I've become quite accustomed to it, and while I haven't decided to continue going to a bow shooting club in real life, I've been really doing plenty of trailer-worthy kills with it. Plus, there's quite a lot of content to unlock and find, with optional loot rooms and branches in the game. The game also has plenty of movement options to allow you to play with, with rail grinding, dashes, double jumps, and slides, which can really make the action feel hectic but fun. The game even gives you boss battles every three levels or so to spice up the runs. A game I would continue to play during hours-long sessions in the future. Absolutely a VR pearl. [i]Key given for QA work on said game.[/i]

Roboquest VR is truly a Flat 2 VR game... quite literally. You can choose to play in a PC-like way with auto reload or maybe full manual reload if you are feeling brave... Currently, there's no benefit to doing thing manually other than it cool. And I think that's a downside. If I reload faster IRL, I shouldn't need to wait for animation to finish. When I first played this game it feels very UEVR-mod kinda way. You are just using controller to point and shoot at thing. And after playing more it still feel like a mod over a standalone game. (Which is okay!) Manual reload still have to wait for animation to finish, when you slash something with your melee you have to wait (like a PC game) If there's weapon that will turn this into a full blown VR game, it gotta be the bow. Bow is just full physical moment like a true VR game. No delay. This is the most fun weapon for me. And second most fun weapon is throwable like Axe, Shuriken. The worst has to be melee. (The bot that can teleport with knife) You slash, it hit enemy, you slash again, it doesn't hit enemy. Ugh! It a co-op game it doesn't have to be THAT balanced. Make it feels good first! It just feels so PC-coded for now. That's all I have about the "Flat (PC) feeling" of the game Now the game itself... is so AWESOME! It's a first roguelike that I can't finish in one day. (Granted I played on hardest difficulty but I also do on other VR titles) This is a FULL LONG PCVR game. You have so much content to enjoy in this game. I haven't even got to experience everything yet! Highly recommend if you love PC game like Risk of Rain 2, Quake, Ultrakill. It got that boomer shooter vibe mixed with roguelike. Any game in VR similar to this?... I don't think so. Nothing has hit the unique vibe of Roboquest yet. Disclaimer: I received this product for free to playtest the game.

This game is great, but the VR port is amazing! The catroonish, cel-shaded graphics "à la Borderlands" is beautiful, movements and interactions are smooth, but what impressed me the most was the level verticality you don't expect (until you unlock the jetpack or the grappling hook) and the amount of weapons: I don't know which other games have such a ginormous choice of deadly items! Also, if you dig deeper this is a game with A TON of things to discover and unlock: perks, characters, collectibles or funny pieces of lore. You can play the game as a great robot shooter, or add hours of fun with all its roguelike elements!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Fantastic VR roguelite shooter — multiplayer is a blast! This was my first time playing Roboquest, and VR turned out to be a great way to experience it. The movement feels smooth, the gunplay is punchy and satisfying, and blasting through runs with a friend is exactly as chaotic and fun as you'd hope. I kept coming back for more sessions — it's got that "one more run" pull that the best roguelites have. What really excites me is where this could go. The core loop is already rock solid, and having co-op in VR is something very few shooters in this space pull off. If the devs keep building on this foundation — smoothing out the multiplayer experience, adding more content over time — this could easily become the go-to co-op VR roguelite. The potential here is huge. Since multiplayer is still fresh, a few friendly notes from our sessions that I hope help the devs polish it up: Session flow could be smoother. It wasn't obvious at first that we needed to head to the camper to actually start a run — we assumed creating a group would kick things off automatically. A small prompt or highlight would help a lot. Room codes are a bit long, and once a session ends, the old code is dead, so we had to spin up a fresh room each time. Shorter, reusable codes would be a quality-of-life win. Also, the join code field placement felt a little unusual compared to most games (it's on the right) — even just a green highlight to draw the eye would help. Reconnecting needs some love. After a lost session (Steam Link paused the game on my end), I got stuck on a loading screen and couldn't rejoin. And when our squad wiped, the host sometimes ended up in a broken state that forced a full session restart. Minor VR polish items: two-handing the Comet Cannon feels awkward (it wants to point straight up), and usernames render in front of the journal log, blocking the text. To the devs: keep it up. The hard part — making the game genuinely fun — is already done, and it shows. I'm invested in seeing this grow, I'll be following updates closely, and I'll be jumping back in as they land. None of these issues stopped us from having a great time. Easy recommend for any VR shooter fan who wants to get in early on something special.
